patch.value: O1 is the simplest architecture satisfying all MUST requirements. The plan assumes an initial target scale of ~1,000 notes (pending Q3 confirmation) which is typically compatible with in-memory processing. A single-process pipeline is easiest to debug, package, and deliver incrementally. Limited extensibility is an acceptable trade-off for the project's focused scope.
Defer active mitigation until Q3 confirms scale; proceed assuming in-memory processing is sufficient for an initial ~1,000-note target, with a checkpoint to revisit if Q3 indicates larger scale.

Candidate B1B delivers a Markdown-to-static-site generator using a monolithic CLI pipeline (O1). The plan follows a thin-slice milestone strategy: Milestone 1 produces a minimal but deployable static site (CLI skeleton, Markdown ingestion, single-note HTML rendering), and each subsequent milestone layers on tags, internal links/backlinks, full-text search, and polish. This architecture minimises upfront design overhead and yields a working artifact from the first milestone, de-risking integration. Key risks around link conventions (K2) and tag conventions (K3) are addressed by requiring explicit configuration before the milestones that depend on them. Scale risks (K4/K5) are deferred pending confirmation of Q3 (expected note scale) and will be validated against R22 during M4. Privacy risk (K8) is accepted with documentation-only mitigation. The candidate targets all 14 MUST requirements and covers SHOULD requirements progressively in later milestones.
